argument_summary: The admissible record supports the locked certification decision only in a narrowed form: operational readiness is evidenced by the aggregate launch-readiness pass of 2.0 percentage points and the absence of severity-one launch-rehearsal incidents, while public governance guidance supports deployment with measured and monitored residual risk plus documented limitations. That is enough to defend certification as a bounded release-readiness decision. It is not enough to defend an unqualified no-disclosure position, because the same admissible record shows a 1.5 percentage-point miss in the insurance claims triage segment, that segment is named in two carrier pilot commitments, legal review is still open, and policy ties materiality to named launch use cases.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-readiness evidence supports proceeding with certification because the release as a whole cleared readiness and rehearsal did not show severity-one failure. That said, business convenience is not the policy basis here, and no separate cost argument is needed to defend the narrowed position.
claims_about_policy: The correct policy claim is narrower than full compliance. On the present admissible record, aggregate readiness evidence can support certification as a caveated governance decision, but it does not resolve the separate disclosure predicate for a named launch use case. The policy text makes clear that non-core or low-volume labels do not settle materiality where customer commitments are named or legal review is pending. Accordingly, the defensible position is not that the no-disclosure path is fully proved; it is that certification can be treated as caveated pending closure of disclosure or formal risk-acceptance handling.
concessions: The present admissible record does not support claiming clean compliance for certification without disclosure resolution or approved risk acceptance.
The insurance claims triage gap affects a named launch use case and therefore fits the policy's materiality trigger on the current record.
Public model-card and general AI-risk guidance support monitoring and documentation, but they do not by themselves override the internal disclosure policy.
